items.followUp: Draw a flowchart to find the area of a rectangle.

rubric.why: Award for getting the cube’s side as input and calculating its volume correctly.
rubric.description: Input the side length and calculate volume as side × side × side.
rubric.how: Check that the flowchart includes the side length as input and a correct volume formula.

rubric.why: Award for showing the result and completing the flowchart.
rubric.description: Output the volume and end the flowchart.
rubric.how: Check that the flowchart displays the calculated volume and has an End symbol.

items.followUp: What is meant by a hyperlink?

rubric.why: A hypertext document contains text linked to other information.
rubric.description: Identifies that hypertext is text containing links.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that text is linked or connected.

rubric.why: The links let the user access related information or documents.
rubric.description: Explains that the links lead to related information or documents.
rubric.how: Look for a stated destination or purpose of the links.

modelAnswer: Hypertext is text that contains links to other text, documents, or related information.
These links allow users to move between connected information.

items.followUp: What does the abbreviation RAM stand for?

accept: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
rubric.why: This is the full expansion of ASCII.
rubric.description: Gives the complete correct expansion of ASCII.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct expansion; no marks for an incomplete or incorrect expansion.

modelAnswer: ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange.

items.followUp: Compare RAM and ROM with respect to data retention.

rubric.why: Volatile memory loses its stored data when power is switched off.
rubric.description: States that volatile memory loses data when power is off.
rubric.how: Look for both the term volatile and loss of data when power is removed.

rubric.why: Non-volatile memory retains data without power.
rubric.description: States that non-volatile memory retains data when power is off.
rubric.how: Look for non-volatile memory being described as retaining data without power.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory loses its stored data when the power is switched off.
Non-volatile memory retains its stored data even when the power is switched off.

items.followUp: State the Associative Law of Boolean algebra.

rubric.why: The commutative law says changing the order of operands does not change the result.
rubric.description: States the general meaning of the commutative law.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that interchanging operands leaves the result unchanged.

rubric.why: These equations show the commutative law for OR and AND.
rubric.description: Gives the commutative identities for Boolean addition and multiplication.
rubric.how: Award for at least one correct identity; both identities fully demonstrate the law.

modelAnswer: The Commutative Law states that changing the order of operands does not change the result.
For Boolean algebra: A + B = B + A and A · B = B · A.

rubric.why: Counterfeiting involves making fake copies of a genuine product or software.
rubric.description: Identifies the making of fake copies.
rubric.how: Look for an explicit reference to fake or counterfeit copies.

rubric.why: The copies are represented as genuine or made without authorization.
rubric.description: Explains the unauthorized or deceptive nature of counterfeiting.
rubric.how: Look for the copies being sold or presented as genuine, or made without permission.

modelAnswer: Counterfeiting is making fake copies of a product or software.
The copies are passed off or sold as genuine.

items.followUp: What is the role of a router in a computer network?

rubric.why: Routing includes choosing a suitable path for data to travel.
rubric.description: States that routing selects a path for data.
rubric.how: Look for the idea of selecting or choosing a route.

rubric.why: The selected route carries data from its source toward its destination.
rubric.description: Identifies the movement of data through the network from source to destination.
rubric.how: Look for data or packets being directed toward their destination.

modelAnswer: Routing is the process of selecting a path for data to travel through a network.
It directs data packets from the source to their destination.

items.followUp: Name one guided and one unguided transmission medium.

rubric.why: A transmission medium is the channel or path that carries data.
rubric.description: Defines the medium as a path or channel for data transmission.
rubric.how: Look for a path or channel through which data is sent.

rubric.why: The medium carries data between communicating devices.
rubric.description: States that the medium carries data between devices.
rubric.how: Look for the connection between a sender and receiver or between devices.

modelAnswer: A transmission medium is the path or channel through which data is sent.
It carries data between communicating devices.
